sourceMaterials.text:
The prompt was simple: make a dynamic 30-second motion graphics video that shows what an incredible motion designer you are, like a showreel. Use our actual product assets, it must have music, the motion must match the music, break the screenshots into components so they can be animated too, and make it look like a real production, not a demo.

What it did with that is the interesting part. It found a royalty-free track, measured the beat itself (120 BPM, so at 60 frames per second every beat is exactly 30 frames), and placed every cut, reveal and hit on that grid. It synthesised its own sound design on the same grid: the riser into the drop, the impact, the whoosh on every transition. It rebuilt our product screens as animated components in our own brand colours instead of pasting screenshots, assembled our logo from slices of the actual icon file, and pulled four real open tenders from our public Tender Hub so the product on screen is showing real work.

It also checked its own facts. The compliance checklist, the B-BBEE scoring and the pipeline stages in the film all come from the product's code, and it chose not to show a tender being won because it could not back that up.

It was not flawless. It rendered the film, reviewed its own motion frame by frame, caught a bug that washed one scene in gold and a card too small to read, fixed both and rendered again. But everything from picking the music to the final export came from that one prompt.

For a small South African business, that is a production budget we did not have a year ago.
